title: How do we build a regular hexagon corner by corner?
description: A side of five centimetres, then a one hundred and twenty degree angle built at each corner by two sixty degree steps, always turning the same way. The sixth side closes the shape. Keeko's doubt, turning the other way at one corner, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same one hundred and twenty degree angle at every corner, turned the same way, closes into a regular hexagon. Watch for students who change the turning direction at a corner.

source: Construct a regular hexagon with side 5 cm using the 120° co
video_script.why: The child builds a hexagon corner by corner, using the one hundred and twenty degree angle just made.
video_script.substitution: The same corner angle and the same side repeat at every corner.
video_script.anchor: A segment AB of 5 cm drawn with a ruler, with a compass beside it.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko turns the other way at C. The path bends back across the figure and does not close into a hexagon.
video_script.payoff_line: The shape has six sides of five centimetres and six angles of one hundred and twenty degrees.

final_answer.value: ABCDEF, with six sides of 5 cm and six angles of 120°
final_answer.spoken: a hexagon with six sides of five centimetres and six angles of one hundred and twenty degrees

maths_rules: Draw AB = 5 cm with the ruler.
At B build 120° from two 60° equal arcs, on the same side each time; cut BC = 5 cm.
Repeat at C, D and E in the same direction to get D, E and F with CD = DE = EF = 5 cm.
Join F to A. Check: FA measures 5 cm with the ruler.
Slip: turning the other way at one corner bends the path back, so it does not close.
video_script.design: One side, one corner rule repeated. The path is drawn turning one way all round. The slip is the reversed turn.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>We want a six sided shape with equal sides and equal angles. Each side is five centimetres, and we start with the side eigh B.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We have a ruler and a compass. We know how to build a one hundred and twenty degree angle.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A six sided shape with equal sides and equal angles is called a regular hexagon.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each of its angles is one hundred and twenty degrees. We make that from two steps of sixty degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks at C we can turn the other way, to the opposite side.
